title: History: since the dawn of civilisation

words.ex: On a class trip to the desert fortresses of Karakalpakstan, two archaeologists let us help sift the sand for pieces of old pottery.
Our history teacher drew a map on the board to show how far Alexander the Great's empire stretched, from Greece all the way to India.
In the fairy tale I read to my little sister, a clever shepherd's daughter saves the whole kingdom from a dragon.
In the museum's Chinese room, every vase is labelled with the dynasty that was in power when it was made.
My parents' first mobile phone, bought at the dawn of the mobile age, was the size of a brick and could only make calls.
My uncle collects coins from every year of Queen Victoria's reign, which lasted almost sixty-four years.
The young prince was the only heir to the throne, so the whole country followed his education closely.
When the head teacher retired after thirty years, everyone wondered who her successor would be.
In our school play, the coronation scene went wrong when the crown slipped down over the new king's eyes.
Our history essay asked whether the conquest of new lands ever brought real benefits to the people who already lived there.
In the library's rare-books room, we were allowed to look at old manuscripts, but only with white cotton gloves on.
In the novel we are reading in class, a poor young peasant who grew up working in the fields leaves his village to study medicine.
The farm hired extra labourers every autumn to dig the ditches and carry the heavy sacks.
Historians have only a few shreds of evidence about how ordinary families lived in the city a thousand years ago.
The small axe in the display case was made by Bronze Age craftsmen, who mixed copper and tin more than three thousand years ago.
Visitors to Carcassonne in southern France can still walk along its medieval walls and towers.
We spent a whole day in Florence admiring paintings by Botticelli and other great artists of the Italian Renaissance.
The museum in Mexico City displays gold jewellery and stone carvings from the pre-colonial era.
With no horses left, the infantry could only advance slowly through the snowy mountains.
In the battle scene of the film, the cavalry galloped down the hill while the foot soldiers waited below.
The knight could hardly climb onto his horse in his heavy suit of armour.
In ancient Egypt, kings rode into battle in light two-wheeled chariots pulled by horses.
My brother spent the whole winter building a model galleon with three masts and tiny paper sails.
Our history teacher explained that in ancient Rome a slave had no rights and could be bought and sold like property.
For years, the remote valley was controlled by a local warlord with his own private army.
In the strategy game, every ruler has to choose between spending gold on bigger armies or on new schools.
As a child, Dilshod dreamed of becoming an explorer and drew maps of imaginary islands in all his notebooks.
In the old trading town, wealthy merchants built large houses with cool cellars where they stored the cloth and spices they traded.
The country still has a monarch, but real power belongs to the elected parliament.
In the past, only members of the nobility were allowed to hunt in the royal forests.
The Indus Valley civilisation built cities with drains and public baths more than four thousand years ago.
Napoleon crowned himself emperor in 1804, with the Pope looking on in Notre-Dame.
Queen Elizabeth II reigned for seventy years, longer than any other British monarch.
When the old king died without a son, his younger brother succeeded to the throne.
Louis XIV became King of France at the age of four but was not crowned until he was fifteen.
The cave paintings near the village were made by Stone Age hunters who had no metal tools at all.
The swords found in the burial mound date from the Iron Age, when smiths had learned to work a metal harder than bronze.
After independence, the post-colonial government renamed many streets that had been named after foreign governors.
Britain passed a law abolishing slavery in most of its colonies in 1833.
France ended its monarchy in 1792 and declared itself a republic.
